subtopic: CUDA / KV Cache access pattern in decode-phase attention
learningObjective: Reason about the memory-access pattern of KV Cache reads during LLM decode-phase attention.
stem: During LLM decoding (one new token per step), the attention kernel loads Q (only 1 token) and reads the full KV Cache. Which statement about the memory-access pattern is correct?

options.text: Decode-phase attention traffic is constant per token regardless of context length; the KV Cache is compressed by the hardware after each step, so HBM reads do not grow.

Decode-phase attention is heavily memory-bound: for each generated token, Q is a single row while K and V (of length S_kv per sequence) must be fully read from HBM. Arithmetic intensity is very low, and per-step HBM traffic scales linearly with S_kv, growing over the sequence.
The KV Cache is fully cached in L2 for any sequence length, so decoding never reads from HBM after the first step; latency is bounded by L2 hit rate.
Decode-phase attention is compute-bound because MMA operations on Q and K/V dominate; the small Q tensor is negligible compared to the compute cost of the matmul.

explanation: Decoding generates one token at a time; Q is only 1 row per head, but K and V of length S_kv per sequence must be fully read from HBM to compute attention. The per-step HBM traffic per (batch, head) is ~2 * S_kv * D * sizeof (K + V) plus small Q/O. Arithmetic intensity is very low — this is a canonical memory-bound step in LLM decoding, and the reason KV Cache size / bandwidth is a first-order concern in serving systems (paged KV cache, KV quantization, MQA/GQA). Per-step cost grows with S_kv, so long-context decoding becomes progressively slower per token.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: no hardware compression; traffic grows with S_kv.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: memory-bound; linear in S_kv per step.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: KV Cache far exceeds L2 for long contexts.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: MMA on 1×D * D×S_kv is memory-bound, not compute-bound.

assumptions: S_kv exceeds L2 cache capacity for real workloads.
nonImplications: Does not imply that KV quantization is the only mitigation; MQA/GQA and paged KV also help.
Does not imply prefill has the same access pattern; prefill is compute-heavy on Q with matmul-shaped patterns.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses prefill and decode compute intensity.

sourceRefs.locator: FlashAttention decoding variants and memory bandwidth analysis

performanceClaim.scope: KV Cache traffic scaling in decode-phase attention
